notes.share_measure: shares are percentages built from domain_days (the month's mean daily share); the MIN_DEN floor applies to the peak-day denominator. domains_peak is not additive across values: se 2019-06 NSEC3 per-value peaks sum to 115% of the _total peak while zones moved from 1 to 5 iterations. Sums over several algorithm values still count a zone or delegation carrying two of them twice (rollovers), which can push a summed share slightly above 100.
notes.strict_panel: every reverse share uses _pooled-afrinic-arin from out/panel_run; per-RIR server-run series are used only for counts (q4 spikes)
notes.reverse_dating: the panel and the ledger are dated one month later than the server run's reverse series; q4 re-dates per-RIR counts +1 month to match (checked in q4.reverse_dating_check)
notes.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.
notes.release_dates: stable release row's `released` from data/software/timelines; default rows use Phase 4 timing_* columns, which already apply first_public_tag

q1_per_program_releases.method: Event = each stable, publicly shipped release, one per calendar month per program. Statistic d3 = mean detrended share in months m..m+2 minus mean in m-3..m-1, detrended by a centred 25-month rolling median (min 13 months). Program statistic = mean d3 over tested release months. Null: the program's release months circularly shifted by one uniform offset within its own span, 1000 draws. Single-release band: 5th-95th percentile of d3 over every testable month of the series.

q3_manual_vs_automatic.method: Actions from delegation_change_clusters (month x source x block x transition). Matching transitions: sign or rollover to the algorithm the default names. Window: the release month and the 3 months after. Statistics: difference, window minus other months, in the share of matching delegations moved in actions of >= 10 delegations, and in the share at level one block or concentrated (delegation_change_levels). Null: the same number of months drawn without replacement from the ledger span, 1000 draws; p = share of draws at or above the observed difference. Sensitivity: the same permutation restricted to months within +-36 months of the window (era-matched), because ledger activity rises about 25-fold from 2009 to 2019.
q3_manual_vs_automatic.proxy_caveat: Action size is a proxy. One operator automating one delegation is indistinguishable from a manual edit, and one operator hand-editing a block is indistinguishable from an upgrade.
q3_manual_vs_automatic.ledger_dating: The ledger and the strict panel are dated by the following month relative to the server run's reverse series (docs/handoff/03_prevalence_metrics.md).

q4_spikes.method: Spikes by program_rfc_cases.spikes() (imported, not re-implemented) on numerator counts: forward per TLD (floor 300), reverse per RIR (floor 30, counts only, re-dated +1 month to match the ledger and panel). Both directions are scanned. A relevant default change maps to the same observable with the same expected direction; 'aligned' = one at 0..3 months before the spike start. Chance = share of the series' months that have a relevant default change 0..3 months before them. Beating chance is judged per observable, corpus and direction by the Poisson-binomial tail of the aligned count.
q4_spikes.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.

q5_successor_rfc.method: Predecessor share in the successor's publication month (checklist publication_date), then the share up to 12 months later (fewer where the corpus ends): 'kept rising' above +10% relative, 'fell' below -10%, else 'flat'. Peak = maximum over the whole covered series; months counted from the successor's publication to the first month after the peak below half of it. Descriptive only.
q5_successor_rfc.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.
